body.statement: On the complete rank-one alternating-factor calibration array with \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}=1/2\), let \(p_t=1+\tfrac12(-1)^t\). In the target chart \(I_{it}\times J_{it}\), the exact formula \(\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}/\psi=\sqrt{(3/4+1/n)\{1/2+4p_t^2/(5n)\}}\) implies \(\inf_{i,t}\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}/\psi>c_{\mathrm{loc}}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\) and \(\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}/\psi\to\sqrt{3/8}\). Direct contraction of the rank-one projector Hessian against the moving-average covariance in that same chart gives \(\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}\,\mathbb E[q_{it}(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon)\mid M]\to-6\sqrt{3/2}\,p_t/(5\sqrt5)\), and therefore \(\psi\,\mathbb E[q_{it}(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon)\mid M]\to\kappa^{\mathrm{drift}}_t=-2\gamma(1)p_t(n/m)(1-\rho_{\mathrm{alt}}^2)/(1+\rho_{\mathrm{alt}}^2)^{3/2}=-12p_t/(5\sqrt5)\) for every fixed parity of \(t\in W\). Thus the global-signal limits are \(-18/(5\sqrt5)\) for even targets and \(-6/(5\sqrt5)\) for odd targets, and \(\psi B_2\to-12/(5\sqrt5)\) because the consecutive window contains equally many targets of each parity. For the native masked optimizer with \(\lambda_n=4\sqrt n\log(n+2)\) and \(\psi=n^{4/5}\), the fitted correction removes this drift and \(n\{(gH)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it})-L-\widehat B_2\}\to_{\mathbb P}0\).
body.justification: The explicit parity constants replace an unsupported universal value and make the early kill test reproducible for the precise mask, factor normalization, dependence law, and penalty used by the native optimizer.
body.gap: Neither the independent-noise MNAR theorem nor fully observed leave-neighbor PCA contains this masked rank-projection coefficient.
body.consumer: A closed-form calibration case detects omitted interior overlap or regularization terms before empirical use.

obligation.what_is_open: Derive the native masked-optimizer and fitted-correction rates needed for the proposition's final assertion that the corrected aggregate remainder is little-o at the inverse-panel scale.
obligation.obstruction: The rank-one Hessian contraction proves the oracle quadratic drift, including its parity constants, but it does not establish that the nonsmooth masked optimizer follows the same expansion uniformly or that the fitted curvature correction is accurate at the inverse-panel scale. Those statements are exactly the unresolved content of the native second-order transfer theorem.
obligation.attempted: The local singular-value ratio, complete three-term derivative, exact serial quadratic contraction, parity average, model-class checks, and rate substitution for a proportional window and signal exponent four fifths were carried out. Proximal nonexpansiveness leaves a bound larger than the inverse-panel scale, so it cannot certify the early kill test.
obligation.partial_result:
For the declared calibration, restriction of the normalized constant left factor to \(I_{it}=C(t)\cup\{i\}\) has squared norm \(3/4+1/n\).  Restriction of the normalized alternating right factor to \(J_{it}=S\cup\{t\}\) has squared norm \(1/2+4p_t^2/(5n)\).  Since the signal is rank one, multiplication of these two restricted norms gives the exact identity
\[
 \frac{\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}}{\psi}
 =\sqrt{\left(\frac34+\frac1n\right)
 \left(\frac12+\frac{4p_t^2}{5n}\right)}
 \longrightarrow\sqrt{\frac38}>\frac12=c_{\mathrm{loc}}.
\]
The completed first-order perturbation inserted into the exact rank-one projector Hessian yields the already calculated covariance contraction
\[
 \psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}\,
 \mathbb E\!\left[
 q_{it}\!\left(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon\right)
 \middle|M\right]
 =-\frac{6\sqrt{3/2}}{5\sqrt5}\,p_t+O(n^{-1}).
\]
Combining it with the preceding local-to-global singular-value ratio gives, for each fixed parity,
\[
 \psi\,
 \mathbb E\!\left[
 q_{it}\!\left(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon\right)
 \middle|M\right]
 \longrightarrow-\frac{12p_t}{5\sqrt5}.
\]
Thus the even and odd limits are \(-18/(5\sqrt5)\) and \(-6/(5\sqrt5)\).  The declared consecutive window has equally many indices of each parity, so
\[
 \psi B_2\longrightarrow-\frac{12}{5\sqrt5}.
\]

The remaining assertion is exactly conditional on the unresolved native-transfer rates.  Put
\[
 \mathcal R_n=\frac1{gH}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it})-L-\widehat B_2.
\]
The decomposition in the native-transfer target would give
\[
 |\mathcal R_n|\le |Q-B_2|+|R_{\mathrm{agg}}|+|\widehat B_2-B_2|.
\]
Here \(H\asymp n\), \(m\asymp n\), \(\psi=n^{4/5}\), \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge\psi/2\), and the asserted pretreatment rate would give \(\Delta_\gamma=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^2n^{-1/2})\).  Direct substitution into the target's raw rates then gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 n|\mathcal R_n|
 &=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \ell_n^4n^{-3/10}
 +\ell_n^4n^{-1/10}
 +\ell_n^4n^{-1/2}
 +\ell_n^2n^{-3/10}
 \right)\\
 &=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the exponent arithmetic and the complete oracle drift calculation, but the native masked-optimizer and fitted-correction bounds used in the last implication remain precisely the unproved content of \(\mathrm{thm:native\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}transfer}\).
